WHAT THE INTERFACE IS: the entry is a hardware client, not a self-contained device object. Its constructor opens four RealSense cameras by hard-coded serial number (franka_fmb_env.py:113-116) and posts open_gripper to http://127.0.0.1:5000/ (lines 64-65, 122-123). step() (197-221) clips a 7-vector, posts a target pose through _send_pos_command (133-137) to the Flask /pose route, and returns the legacy four-tuple; /pose publishes geometry_msgs/PoseStamped on /cartesian_impedance_controller/equilibrium_pose (franka_server.py:298-303 and 145-153, publisher 42-46). The prerequisites are ROS Noetic, a Franka Panda or Franka Research 3 arm and gripper, libfranka and franka_ros (robot_infra/README.md:13-16); the server launches roslaunch serl_franka_controllers (franka_server.py:65-77). No simulator, mock, upstream test or recorded session exists in the clone: the card's upstream-sim hint points at Transformer/orca/model/tokenizers.py:472 DummyTaskTokenizer, a policy tokenizer, not a robot simulator.

WHY THERE IS NO HONEST STOP (the blocker): the entry class FrankaFMB has no stop, halt, pause, abort or e-stop member. The only stop-like route is the server's /stopimp (franka_server.py:231-234), which calls stop_impedance (79-82) and only terminates the impedance-controller subprocess; the env class neither calls it nor exposes it, and no line of the clone documents the arm's state after that termination, braking, gravity compensation or any confirmation of quiescence. recover() posts /clearerr (franka_fmb_env.py:130-131, franka_server.py:84-87) and is fault clearing, which the rules forbid as a stop and require inside a re-enable action. go_to_rest()/reset() are motions (franka_fmb_env.py:272-356; reset blocks on input() at 349-350). close() only closes the cameras and is itself broken (self.cap.items, 418-419). The README's request table even swaps the startimp and stopimp descriptions (robot_infra/README.md:54-55), so it is not evidence of a safe stop either.

RISK AND SAFE-045: the device is a Franka robot arm, which the task's safety rule places at least at R2 (high energy and contact hazard; the card's risk_floor is R0 but the device's hazard sets R2). A hardware R2 driver needs an independent stop: estop_physical_ref (a path:LINE of an independent hardware e-stop in the clone) or an @action(safe_state=True) (SAFE-045, MHS/spec/04-safety.md:376-382). The clone documents no physical e-stop line; the README only links to external Franka FCI documentation (robot_infra/README.md:16), which is not a citation. The only native actions available for a safe-state action are a motion (go_to_rest), a gain change (precision_mode/compliance_mode), a bounding-box change, or a camera close; none stops motion, and a fake that said it had stopped would invent the protection. The card's PythonObjectDriver cannot express the stop either and no SDK helper supplies one. This is not HELPER_MISSING (a direct Driver over the entry has the same missing stop) and not ENTRY_UNVERIFIED (the entry exists).

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK: a source-backed stop on the entry or server with a fresh read-back that confirms quiescence (not a cached pose), or a cited physical e-stop in the clone, plus a recording or an upstream mock for the fake; a human transcript of a real run would also be needed. Until then no honest fake exists and the primary control cannot be published.
